From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: FWD Health — DPA redlines and SCCs questions

Jordan — thanks for the flag and the quick turnaround. I reviewed the customer's track-changes and attached an annotated response (internal_dpa_response_v1.docx). High level: we can close this quickly if we follow a tight give/take. Summary of recommended positions and concessions below.

1) SCCs / Transfer addendum: Accept the 2021 SCCs and add an explicit transfer impact addendum referencing UK adequacy steps. Ask: include an audit covenant (reasonable cooperation) and limit any long-tail indemnity for historical transfers to cases of willful misconduct.

2) Roles (controller/processor): We should keep our standard language that Redwood is processor for the inference service and controller only for telemetry used for product improvement (with opt-outs). Customer asks to flip portions; we must not take controller status for customer-provided PHI or regulated datasets. Proposed compromise: carve out "regulated datasets" and add a definition + obligation that customer designates any data subject to special regulation at time of onboarding.

3) Subprocessor notice: 30 days' notice is reasonable; we can offer 30 days' notice for non-security-critical subs and immediate notice for critical security subprocessors. Also propose a quarterly public subprocessor list and a private list on request (NDA).

4) CMK/HSM: Karthik, need your confirmation. Operationally, we do have a CMK/HSM path for Dedicated and Private deployments today; hosted customers can be offered an HSM-backed option as a dedicated add-on with ~6-8 week lead time to configure and validate per account. If we can offer that as an add-on (billing/implementation), I will suggest language: "Customer may elect CMK/HSM for an additional implementation fee; Redwood will provide project timeline and security review."

5) Retention: 13 months for non-production telemetry is probably OK with a technical caveat. For logs used in model improvement/training derivatives we must keep a short retention for debugging; propose: 13 months for aggregated telemetry, 90 days for request-level logs used for model training unless Customer opts out in writing.

6) Remedies & SLA: Customer requests broader termination/return wording. We should keep our standard return/wipe obligations, and offer an accelerated export window (30 days) as a commercial concession if they sign a 12-month committed term.

Commercial asks to consider a one-time implementation credit in exchange for accepting our default retention and controller/processor carveouts.

Next steps:
- Karthik: confirm CMK/HSM availability and typical lead time (please reply in-thread).
- Ben: recommend concedes/credits and a go-to-market sweetener we can offer to close this (credit, pilot discount, or short-term SLA commitment).
- Jordan: if you can propose a 30-minute call Wed or Thur with their counsel and procurement, I'll prepare the annotated DPA and a short summary deck.

I'll attach the internal response and mark the clauses we recommend for negotiation. If we accept the add-on HSM approach and the 13/90-day split for retention, the rest is mostly language tuning.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
